narrative: This was an emergency vendoring of dolthub/driver to remove telemetry. The reviewer swept the whole vendored tree every round, re-raising upstream issues (example/main.go, data_source_test, QuerySplitter, the dolt/go pin) that the agent consistently and correctly declined under its minimal-diff rule. The one place the agent broke that rule, F2's result.go fix, left closeErr untranslated, which became F10 and needed its own round. The dolt/go pin skew was raised four times because the round-0 pushback came without the cheap acknowledging comment that was added only later.
guidance_observations: Decide the scope rule for vendored code once, before replying to any thread, and apply it uniformly; the one exception (F2) was the only fix that produced a follow-on finding.
A declined-but-real observation is best closed with a one-line in-code acknowledgement in the same round; leaving the code unchanged invites the reviewer to re-raise it every round.
F1's plan-then-revert cost a full test cycle that checking the vendor scope rule first would have avoided.

guidance_observations: The agent checked the action's real definition rather than arguing from the reviewer's text, which is the right move for claims about an external action's interface.

narrative: This PR regenerated the code-review workflow from the installer template. The reviewer's blocking 'checkout@v6 does not exist' came from a model knowledge cutoff, and the agent refuted it with a real run log. timeout-minutes was accepted through the template, and issues:write was deferred. Round 1 re-raised the v6 claim and added a belt-and-suspenders fork gate that got no reply.
guidance_observations: Replies went into a single issue comment rather than onto each thread, so two round-1 threads were resolved with no recorded reasoning.
Changing the template and regenerating, rather than hand-editing the generated workflow, was the correct route for the accepted timeout finding.

guidance_note: When widening an accept pattern, enumerate the new multi-match combinations it admits (e.g. LICENSE-APACHE + LICENSE-MIT) and decide how the selection step treats each before pushing.

guidance_note: When adding an 'ambiguous → error' branch, list every name the matcher accepts as a canonical bare file (LICENSE, LICENCE, COPYING, UNLICENSE) and test each one paired with a sibling file.

narrative: This PR added a license-bundle generator. Widening the license filename regex for F2 turned a loud failure for dual-license modules into a silent pick (F3). F3's fix, an ambiguity error, kept the bare-name preference as a literal 'LICENSE' check. That broke LICENCE (F9, F10) and then COPYING/UNLICENSE (F11), each needing its own round, until the agent made the regex alternation and the preference check share one definition. The other findings were independent improvements to pre-review code, plus one speculative cosmetic change (F5) that should have been declined.
guidance_observations: The chain came from two independently maintained lists of the same name set; deriving the preference check from the regex's alternation in the F3 fix would have saved rounds 3 and 4.
Each fix to the matcher was tested only on the shape the reviewer named; a table over every accepted root name would have caught LICENCE and COPYING before review.
The agent's F11 reply named the root cause ('two independently-maintained lists') and fixed the class; that analysis was available at F3.

evidence: The hunk shows ensureQuarantineTable's own create branch also executes DDL without committing, and the review summary confirms the caller commits immediately afterwards. narrative: This was a small self-heal fix for a stale-shaped quarantine table, approved in one round. Both advisories asked for patterns the package deliberately does not use (per-helper commits, fault-injection tests), and the agent declined both with references to the file's existing conventions.
guidance_observations: The pushbacks named concrete sibling call sites (schema_reconcile.go:164, 830, 864) as evidence of the convention, which makes them checkable rather than asserted.

evidence: alterAddColumnRe skipped ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS and multi-column forms silently. guidance_note: When a regex extracts targets from free text, assert in the original commit that the parsed count equals a literal-keyword count, so an unparsed form fails loudly instead of being skipped.

narrative: This PR added detection of goose version-slot reuse. One advisory about silently skipped DDL forms was answered with a count assertion rather than a fuller parser, and the work uncovered a sharper false-capture bug. The second round was clean.
guidance_observations: Writing the test for the reviewer's case surfaced a worse bug than the one reported; testing the reviewer's exact input before declaring a fix paid off here.

narrative: This PR turned version-content drift into a checkpointed self-repair. Round 0's escaping edge case was handled with the doc-only mitigation the reviewer offered, consistent with sibling scanners. Round 1, triggered by that doc commit, raised a speculative empty-repair guard, which the agent rejected with a precise precondition argument.
guidance_observations: Round 1 existed only because a doc-only commit re-triggered review; its finding was on unchanged code.
